Fix the remaining "reports success without verifying it" defects in the Nxeon hosting platform at /opt/nxeon. This is the defect class the whole codebase is organised against, and these are the surviving instances on the operations side. Findings come from a customer-journey rehearsal in `docs/QA-JOURNEY.md` (read H4, H5 and M7) and from the honesty inventory in `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` ("Known gaps — the honest inventory", the "Still not true" table). Verify each against the current source before changing anything — one recent audit reported a live money bug that turned out to be a stale comment, so read code, not prose.

**H4 — automatic backups can silently never exist while the UI shows a fresh timestamp every night.** `lastAutoBackup` is stamped when the job is ENQUEUED, not when a backup demonstrably exists. So a customer sees "last backup: today" indefinitely while nothing has ever been written, and finds out at restore time. Stamp it from proof — the backup actually existing in storage — and make the absence visible rather than invisible.

**H5 — `syncPortForwards` flushes the whole NAT chain and rebuilds it unverified.** A flush-and-rebuild that is never checked afterwards can leave every customer's port forwarding dead with nothing reporting a problem. Verify the resulting ruleset actually contains what was intended, and fail loudly if not. Be careful: this touches live networking on the production host, so reason about what happens mid-flush and make the failure mode "we tell you it broke", never "we left it broken and said nothing".

**"Game auto-update cannot fail"** — `worker/game-update.ts:60` returns `set -e; ${steam}${restart}; true`. steamcmd is `|| true` (`:51`) and skipped entirely when absent; every restart branch is `|| true` (`:59`); the command ends `; true`. The remote command CANNOT exit non-zero, so `:134` always reports "The latest server update was applied and the service was restarted." This runs unattended every 6 hours. `worker/apps.ts` is the model for the fix — it makes every app declare what its install PROVES and then HTTP-probes to confirm, and an exit code of 0 is never accepted as evidence.

**M7 — the other missing verification gates** listed in `docs/QA-JOURNEY.md`. Work through them and apply the same standard.

The house rule, which this engine's own comments state repeatedly: a surface must never report an outcome it did not verify. Where you cannot prove success, say so precisely — with the reason and the command the operator or customer can run — rather than downgrading to a cheerful guess. `wp_die()` prints its error and exits 0; an exit code is not proof. Prefer refusing over guessing.

VERIFY, reporting only what you observed:
- `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit ; echo "exit=$?"` — must be 0.
- `cd /opt/nxeon && npm test` — currently 174/174; must stay green, and ADD tests. Follow the style of `test/migration-gate.test.ts`: extract the decision logic as exported pure functions, drive side-effectful things through a seam with an in-memory fake (see `UnitExecHost`), keep tests free of SSH/network/clock, and put each real incident in a comment above its test.
- Where a change affects generated shell, that shell must still parse: `test/migration-gate.test.ts` runs `sh -n` and `dash -n` over `srcInventoryScript` for exactly this reason. A quoting mistake in generated shell fails on a customer's live server, not in a build.
- Do not run destructive operations against production. Do not restart production services. If you need to exercise networking or backups, use STAGING (`nxeon-staging-worker`) or a throwaway target, and say plainly which findings you RAN versus only READ.

Do NOT edit: `lib/actions.ts`, `components/AuthForms.tsx`, `lib/order.ts`, `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts`, `app/api/stripe/**`, `worker/migrate.ts`, `worker/migrate-real.ts`, `docs/QA-JOURNEY.md`, `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` — other agents own those. Do not deploy or commit.

Report: each defect with the evidence line you checked, what now constitutes proof for each surface, what you RAN versus READ, test output, and anything found but not fixed.

1	# QA — Full customer journey rehearsal
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-07-26
4	**Environment driven:** staging (`nxeon-staging-web` :3001, nginx :8080 / `https://staging.nxeon.cloud`, DB `nxeon_staging`, `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`)
5	**Production touched:** read-only `GET` on public marketing pages only. No Stripe charge, no VM create/destroy, no DNS/OVH change, no outbound mail to a real person.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 0. Method, and a caveat that affects how you read this
10	
11	Every finding below is tagged:
12	
13	- **[RAN]** — I drove it over real HTTP/a real browser and watched it happen.
14	- **[READ]** — I traced the code path and did not execute it. Never presented as an observed result.
15	
16	Test accounts created on staging: `dana.quill2@example.com`, `sam.card@example.com`, `sam.two@example.com`. Six sandbox servers and ~$1,500 of play money. All disposable.
17	
18	### Caveat: staging is 21 commits behind production
19	
20	`/opt/nxeon-staging` is at `8c8b7d9`; `/opt/nxeon` is at `fd71056`. Twenty-one commits apart, including several that touch exactly what I was asked to test (wallet floor, proration symmetry, Stripe-provision coupling, coupons, notification prefs, sidebar).
21	
22	So for **every** finding I observed on staging I diffed the responsible file against the production tree and said which applies. Where the file is byte-identical I say so explicitly. **This staleness is itself a launch-readiness problem**: the environment built to rehearse the release does not contain the release. Re-run `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` before trusting staging for anything else.
23	
24	---
25	
26	## LAUNCH BLOCKERS
27	
28	### B1. The wizard charges the customer when they click "Continue →", four steps before the confirmation screen
29	
30	**[RAN]** — reproduced 5 times, 5 servers created, 5 wallet debits.
31	`components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:646-661` — **byte-identical in staging and production.**
32	
33	On the **Access** step, type a valid hostname and click **Continue →**. Instead of advancing to Review, the order is placed immediately: a `Next-Action` POST to `payAndDeploy`, wallet debited, VM provisioned, browser redirected to the new server's page.
34	
35	The customer never sees the Review step. They never choose a billing term (it commits at the `default_term`, currently Monthly). They never see "Due today". There is no confirmation of any kind between clicking a button labelled *Continue* and money leaving their wallet.
36	
37	Verified ledger from one such click:
38	
39	```
40	-629  Order: Starter VPS (qa-probe-02) — Monthly · Summer Sale 30% off first term
41	```
42	
43	**Root cause** (**[READ]**, following from the observed behaviour): the two buttons are branches of an unkeyed ternary in the same DOM position.
44	
45	```jsx
46	{!isLast ? (
47	  <button type="button" ... onClick={() => setStep((s) => s + 1)}>Continue →</button>
48	) : (
49	  <button className="btn-primary px-6" disabled={pending || !canDeploy} ...>   // no type → submit
50	)}
51	```
52	
53	React reconciles both branches onto the **same `<button>` element** and patches its attributes. `setStep` runs inside the click handler, React re-renders synchronously, and `type="button"` is removed from the very node the browser is still processing the click for. The browser then performs its default action — submit. It only fires when `canDeploy` is true, which is why an **empty** hostname reaches Review correctly and a **filled** one does not. That is the whole bug.
54	
55	- Wallet-funded customer: **charged with no confirmation screen.**
56	- Zero-balance card customer **[RAN]**: `payAndDeploy` returns a `checkoutUrl`, but the redirect is gated on `submittedRef` which the Deploy button never got to set — so the redirect is suppressed and the customer lands on Review looking normal. No charge, no visible damage, but a stray Stripe Checkout session per traversal.
57	
58	**Smallest fix:** add distinct `key` props (`key="continue"` / `key="deploy"`) so React unmounts one and mounts the other, and give the deploy button an explicit `type="submit"`.
59	
60	---
61	
62	### B2. "Renew now (+30 days, $8.99)" charged $97.09 and added 12 months
63	
64	**[RAN]** — clicked it, watched the debit and the date move.
65	`components/SubscriptionControls.tsx:35,90` (display) vs `lib/actions.ts:629-654` (charge). **`SubscriptionControls.tsx` is byte-identical in staging and production.**
66	
67	On a Starter server bought on an annual term:
68	
69	| | |
70	|---|---|
71	| Button label | `Renew now (+30 days, $8.99)` |
72	| Confirmation dialog | **none** — one click, immediate debit |
73	| Actual charge | **$97.09** (`-9709` in `WalletTransaction`) |
74	| Paid-until before | 2027-07-26 |
75	| Paid-until after | **2028-07-26** |
76	
77	The card is handed `server.plan.priceCents` — a **monthly** figure — and hardcodes the string "+30 days", while `renewNow` prices `vpsTermPriceCents(plan.priceCents, server.termMonths)` and advances `addMonths(base, term.months)`.
78	
79	A **10.8×** overcharge here. On Max/36-month it is `$32.99` shown against `$950.11` charged — **28.8×**. No dialog, no undo.
80	
81	**Smallest fix:** `lib/stripe-cards.ts:124` already exports `renewalCharge(server, prices)` — the exact function `worker/billing.ts` renews with. Compute it in `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`, pass `{totalCents, months}` into `RenewalCard`, and build the label from those. Add a confirm dialog stating the amount.
82	
83	---
84	
85	### B3. The site-wide promo bar advertises a price no plan has — live on production right now
86	
87	**[RAN]** — fetched `https://nxeon.cloud/` and `/pricing`.
88	`components/marketing/PromoBar.tsx:19` — `const exampleRegular = 500;`
89	
90	Every marketing page carries:
91	
92	> Summer Sale · **30% off your first term** — VPS from ~~$5~~ **$3.50/mo**, renews at $5/mo.
93	
94	The cheapest active plan is **Starter $8.99 → $6.29**. There is no $5 plan; the only sub-$8.99 row in the DB is `nano`, and it is `active = false`. So the headline number is **80% below** anything purchasable, and the same page renders the real grid a few hundred pixels lower — the contradiction is visible in one screenshot.
95	
96	The comment directly above the constant claims the opposite of what the code does: *"show the honest first-term price so the bar's headline number matches what checkout charges."*
97	
98	**Smallest fix:** derive it — `const exampleRegular = Math.min(...activePlans.map(p => p.priceCents))` — or delete the "from $X" clause and keep only the percentage.
99	
100	---
101	
102	### B4. There is no email verification anywhere in the product
103	
104	**[RAN]** — registered `dana.quill2@example.com`, was signed in and on `/dashboard` immediately.
105	`lib/actions.ts:115-139`; **no `emailVerified` field and no verification-token model exist in `prisma/schema.prisma`.**
106	
107	`register()` creates the user, calls `createSession()`, best-effort sends a welcome email, and redirects to `/dashboard`. Anyone can sign up with **any** address, including one they do not control, and immediately transact.
108	
109	For a hosting business this is the account-recovery and abuse-control foundation: signup-credit and referral farming across throwaway addresses (`grantSignupCredit` / `maybeRewardReferral` both fire on an unverified account), and a mistyped address means invoices, root passwords and dunning notices go to a stranger with no way to recover.
110	
111	**Smallest fix:** ship a `User.emailVerifiedAt` + token table, gate *ordering* (not login) on it, and reuse the existing `PasswordResetToken` mail plumbing.
112	
113	---
114	
115	## HIGH — money and trust
116	
117	### H1. The term cards state a recurring price that will never be charged
118	
119	**[RAN]** — read verbatim off the running Review step.
120	`components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:544-563`
121	
122	```
123	−10%  Annual   $5.66/mo   $67.96 billed every 1 yr
124	−20%  Triennial $5.03/mo  $181.24 billed every 3 yr
125	```
126	
127	"$67.96 billed every 1 yr" is the **promo first-term** price. Renewals bill the regular price — `$97.09` — which I confirmed by actually renewing (B2). `currentPromo()` never returns null (`LAUNCH_SALE`, 15%, `lib/promotions.ts:58-65`), so this is wrong on **100% of orders, 100% of the time**.
128	
129	The disclosure below it — *"30% off your first term applied — renews at the regular price"* — carries no number and no date, and the strikethrough regular total appears only on the "Due today" row, not on the card that says *billed every*.
130	
131	`components/marketing/PricingGrid.tsx:110` gets this exactly right (*"First term. Renews at $8.99/mo."*). Copy that.
132	
133	**Smallest fix:** `{money(total)} first term · renews at {money(regTotal)}` — `regTotal` is already in scope at line 544.
134	
135	### H2. Stripe order confirm re-prices after the card is charged and takes the difference from the wallet
136	
137	**[READ]** — `lib/actions.ts:391-430` → `lib/stripe.ts:41` → `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts:70-80` → `lib/order.ts:158,188,197`
138	
139	The Checkout session metadata carries the *intent*, never the quoted total, so `placeOrder` re-runs `orderQuote` at confirm time — including a fresh `currentPromo(new Date())`. If the promo rotates between checkout creation and the Stripe redirect, the recomputed total is debited from the wallet with no new consent. With no balance: payment captured, no server, and a notification reading *"Payment received — we couldn't finish setting up your server."*
140	
141	This is an inconsistency rather than an oversight in principle: `lib/resize.ts:115` and `lib/disk-expand.ts:153` already take the amount from Stripe metadata precisely so confirm cannot re-price. The order path is the one that missed it.
142	
143	**Smallest fix:** add `c: quote.chargeCents` to the `nxeonOrder` metadata and give `placeOrder` an optional `chargeCents` override, mirroring `applyResize`.
144	
145	### H3. A card-paid purchase produces two PAID invoices and doubles "Paid · lifetime"
146	
147	**[READ]** — `lib/stripe.ts:230-239`, `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts:70`, `app/dashboard/invoices/page.tsx:23-25,38`
148	
149	`creditCheckoutSession` writes a PAID *"Wallet top-up"* invoice for every paid session, then the order branch writes its own. An $82.53 annual purchase shows as `Wallet top-up $82.53` + `Starter VPS — Annual $82.53`, and the invoices page reports **$165.06** paid lifetime.
150	
151	Each document is internally consistent (`lib/invoices.ts:139-163` derives totals from line items), so nothing is fabricated — but a customer reconciling against their card statement sees twice their spend. `worker/billing.ts:615-617` already states the correct rule for the renewal path.
152	
153	**[RAN] counter-check:** for **wallet-paid** orders and renewals the invoices reconcile *exactly* with the ledger — 7 invoices, 7 wallet rows, amounts identical including the $97.09 renewal. The defect is specific to the Stripe leg.
154	
155	### H4. Automatic backups can silently never exist while the UI shows a fresh timestamp every night
156	
157	**[READ]** — `worker/backup-schedule.ts:55-61`, `worker/index.ts:745-768,979-985`; customer-facing at `components/customer/BackupSchedule.tsx:103-105`
158	
159	`lastAutoBackup` is stamped **when the job row is enqueued**, not when the backup succeeds — and it is written nowhere else. `backupCreate` gates the vzdump task's exit status but never checks the archive exists or is non-zero, has no failure notification, and is excluded from `VM_STATE_FAILURE_JOBS`.
160	
161	So "Last automatic backup: 2026-07-26 04:00 UTC" means *a row was created*. vzdump could have failed every night for a month with no alert, and the schedule is marked satisfied so the retry is a full interval away. Discovered at restore time — the one moment it cannot be fixed.
162	
163	Aggravating: the deploy wizard **sells** this at the point of sale (**[RAN]** — Add-ons step reads *"Daily auto-backups · Included · Nightly snapshots to separate storage for easy restore"*).
164	
165	**Smallest fix:** drop the `lastAutoBackup` write in `backup-schedule.ts` (the in-flight de-dupe at :50-53 already prevents pile-up) and set it in `backupCreate` after a storage-content read shows a fresh volid with `size > 0`. Add a failure `notify`.
166	
167	### H5. `syncPortForwards` flushes the whole NAT chain and rebuilds it unverified
168	
169	**[READ]** — `worker/network.ts:28-55`
170	
171	Line 30 unconditionally runs `iptables -t nat -F NXEON_FWD`, then rebuilds per-server in a loop with no try/catch, no rollback and no `-C` read-back. `exec` here is `promisify(execFile)`, so **one** failed `-A` rejects and aborts the loop — every server after that point is left with no DNAT rule. The job still goes DONE, because DONE means "the last `iptables -A` exited 0".
172	
173	Fleet-wide SSH blackhole, no notification, dashboard still showing everyone's port. `remove()` (`worker/index.ts:401`) calls this *after* deleting the server row, so a throw re-queues DELETE, which then dies on "Server not found" and never retries the sync.
174	
175	**Smallest fix:** build into a scratch chain and swap atomically; at minimum collect per-rule failures instead of aborting, then assert each server's rule with `iptables -t nat -C`.
176	
177	### H6. Any customer who enables 2FA is permanently locked out
178	
179	**[READ]** — `components/AuthForms.tsx:97` vs `lib/actions.ts:149,169`
180	
181	The login email input is **uncontrolled** while the password beside it is controlled. React 19 resets uncontrolled fields on every `<form action={fn}>` submit. So: correct credentials → server returns `needs2fa: true` → React blanks the email → user types the code → `credsSchema` fails on the now-empty email → `"Invalid email or password."` without `needs2fa`, so the code field unmounts. Forever.
182	
183	**Smallest fix:** make the email input controlled — the same one-line pattern already used for the password.
184	
185	### H7. A capitalised email at signup makes password reset silently impossible
186	
187	**[READ]** — `lib/actions.ts:87,146` vs `lib/actions-account.ts:112,120`
188	
189	Register and login store/query the address verbatim; Postgres `@unique` is case-sensitive. Forgot-password lowercases first. `Alice@Example.com` therefore never matches, and the (correctly non-enumerating) response still says *"If an account exists for that email, a reset link is on its way."* No mail, no error, no recourse. Mobile keyboards auto-capitalise the first letter.
190	
191	**Smallest fix:** `.toLowerCase()` on the register and login lookups.
192	
193	---
194	
195	## MEDIUM — dead ends and false success
196	
197	### M1. The Deploy button is greyed out with no explanation
198	
199	**[RAN]** — Playwright reported `<button disabled class="btn-primary px-6">Deploy — paid from wallet</button>`.
200	`components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:205,650`
201	
202	Skip the hostname (it sits between two fields *explicitly* marked "optional" and carries no required marker), and **Continue → is not gated** — you reach Review, see `Hostname —`, and the Deploy button is disabled with **no message anywhere** saying why. `canDeploy` folds four conditions into one silent boolean.
203	
204	Four steps back from the cause, on the last screen of the funnel.
205	
206	**Smallest fix:** gate Continue on the Access step, and render the reason next to the disabled button.
207

case. `ENABLE_REAL_MIGRATION=1` (`.env:35`) today, so it is dormant — **one lost `.env` line re-creates

`ENABLE_REAL_CPANEL` workers (`websites.ts:39`, `apps.ts:81`, `databases.ts:35`, `services.ts:34`);
`ENABLE_REAL_CPANEL=1` (`.env:36`), so those are dormant on the same terms.

**6. Nxeon-registered domains get no mail DNS.** *PARTIAL — the UI promises otherwise.*
`components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx:286` tells the customer that a domain registered with Nxeon has
*"its mail DNS … managed for you — mailboxes go live automatically."* Nothing publishes
MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC at name.com: `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts:283` only ever adds A records. Their mail
will not work, and the panel says it will. The deliverability check rendered directly beneath that
sentence will correctly report the records as missing — which is the panel contradicting itself on one
screen.

**7. `email_mx_host` and `email_spf_include` change nothing.** *SAVED-BUT-UNREAD.*
The panel no longer lies about it — both fields now carry `note="Not wired — and this value disagrees
with the … that panel actually publishes."` and hedged hints (`components/admin/settings/
GeneralPanel.tsx:111`, `:119`) — but editing either still has no effect. The real values are hardcoded
at `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:36` (`mail.nxeon.cloud`) and `:41` (`nxeon.cloud`). The comment at
`GeneralPanel.tsx:96-105` records why this must not be wired naively: the stored values disagree with
what the platform actually publishes, so wiring them without first reconciling them would hand every
customer DNS records that do not work **and** make the deliverability self-check fail correct setups.
Reconcile first, wire second.

**8. Domain-ownership verification and the DNS tools use the wrong resolver.** *PARTIAL.*
`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:5` imports the top-level `resolveTxt`/`resolveMx`, used at `:464` and
`:474` — so verification runs against `/etc/resolv.conf` (OVH's cache), not the zone's authority. A
customer who has just published `_nxeon-verify` can be told it is not there.
`lib/mail/deliverability.ts` does it correctly and is the model to copy. The same bug is in
`app/api/tools/dns/route.ts:35` (a `Resolver` with no `setServers`) and
`app/api/tools/my-ip/route.ts:23` (`reverse` on the default resolver).

**9. There is no PTR / reverse-DNS check anywhere.** *Missing.*
`checkDeliverability` covers only `mx | spf | dkim | dmarc` (`lib/mail/deliverability.ts:41`) — despite
the motivating incident being a *reverse* lookup. There is no `reverse(` call and no `PTR` query
anywhere in `lib/mail/deliverability.ts` or `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts`. The check itself is no
longer orphaned — `checkEmailDeliverability` (`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:523`) is now called from
`components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx:579` — so the missing piece is the PTR row, not the entry point.
`components/admin/MailAnalytics.tsx:135-148`'s "DNS & DMARC" card is still static prose, not a check.

**10. Cloudflare connections cannot refresh.** *PARTIAL.* The working scope in `.env:39`
(`dns.read dns.write zone.read`) omits `offline_access`, so Cloudflare issues no refresh token and every
connection dies at `expiresAt` (`lib/cloudflare-oauth.ts:332` → `CF_RECONNECT`) with no re-auth prompt.
Separately the **code default** scope (`:59`, `zone:read dns_records:edit offline_access`) is a value
Cloudflare rejects, so any deploy that loses that env var reintroduces the "invalid scope" error a
customer hit three times. The two are not interchangeable: one refreshes and is rejected, the other is
accepted and cannot refresh.

**11. ⚠ USER ACTION — platform transactional email is unsigned.** *Live risk, needs a human.*
`dkim._domainkey.nxeon.cloud` is **NXDOMAIN**, verified against a public resolver (1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8,
not the local cache — see gap 8 for why that distinction matters). Every message the platform sends —
password resets, invoices, dunning warnings, suspension notices — is therefore **DKIM-unsigned** and
lands in spam or is dropped outright at the large providers. A stale `nxeon._domainkey.nxeon.cloud`
**is** still published and resolves, which makes this look configured at a glance; it is the wrong
selector and signs nothing.

Fix: take the key for selector `dkim` from **Mailcow's API** — mail is Mailcow's, and the local
resolver must not be trusted for this — publish it at `dkim._domainkey.nxeon.cloud`, then **delete**
the stale `nxeon._domainkey` record. Re-verify against a public resolver, not `dig` with no `@server`.

**12. ⚠ USER ACTION — every backup exists on exactly one chassis.** *Not configured, honestly reported.*
`OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET` and `OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE` in `/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env` are both unset —
the file contains nothing but comments — so `scripts/backup-offsite.sh:101-125` writes
`{"ok":false,"configured":false,"kind":"none","detail":"no OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE or
OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET set"}` to `/tank/backup/status/offsite.json` and exits non-zero. That leaves
`nxeon-backup-offsite.service` in a **deliberate `failed` state** (confirmed: `failed`, since
2026-07-26 06:35 UTC) so the gap is visible in `systemctl` rather than silent.

`/tank` is one pool in one chassis. A chassis loss loses every customer backup **and** the platform's
own disaster-recovery set. Set exactly one of the two variables — not both, which the script refuses at
`:129` — and the timer starts replicating.

**13. A genuinely in-use volume cannot be force-detached.** *PARTIAL.* The worker supports an informed
override via `payload.ackInUse` (`worker/volumes.ts:1146-1147`, honoured at `:1177`, `:1189`, `:1211`)
and the refusal notification tells the customer to *"confirm the forced detach in the dashboard"* — but
**nothing sets it**: `ackInUse` appears in `worker/volumes.ts` and nowhere else in the tree. Not
`lib/actions-volumes.ts`, not `components/customer/Volumes.tsx`. The escape hatch exists only in the
engine, and the notification points at a control that does not exist.

**14. Volumes are not portable.** *PARTIAL — the framing is stronger than the code.*
`lib/actions-volumes.ts:129` refuses attaching to any server other than `volume.serverId`, and detach
only clears it when the disk did not stay behind (`worker/volumes.ts:1154`). Once a volume holds data it
is effectively pinned to its first server.

**15. "Restore failed — your server is unaffected" is false for restores.** *UNVERIFIED SUCCESS,
inverted.* `components/customer/BackupControls.tsx:134` renders `{verb} failed — your server is
unaffected` and `:147` adds *"No changes were made to your running server. You can safely try again."*
— with `verbFor` (`:16`) returning `"Restore"` for `BACKUP_RESTORE`. By the time a restore fails,
`worker/restore.ts:125` has already stopped the VM and step 2 has begun overwriting its disk with
`qmrestore --force`. **The most reassuring message in the product appears in its most destructive
failure case.**

**16. Game settings are switched off and the copy has not caught up.** *PARTIAL.*
`ENABLE_REAL_GAMECFG` is absent from `.env`, so every production save now fails loudly
(`worker/game-config.ts:86`) — correct, but the feature is non-functional while

**17. The capacity gauge is a model, and it gates deploys.** *PARTIAL.*
`lib/capacity.ts:15` uses `NXEON_HOST_RAM_MB ?? 64000` and the variable is unset in `.env`, so the
ceiling is a hardcoded assumption about this specific box. `capacitySnapshot()` (`:46`) sums **plan** RAM
across servers on **all** nodes against that single-host ceiling, while the platform is multi-node. It
is shown to customers at `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx:26` and it **gates purchases** via
`capacityCheck` (`lib/capacity.ts:69`) at `lib/order.ts:164`, `lib/actions.ts:258` and
`lib/actions-gameplans.ts:221` — so the number is load-bearing on the money path.

**18. The public status page reports `web` as a constant.** *PARTIAL.*
`lib/monitoring.ts:326` hardcodes `web: { status: "operational", detail: "serving requests" }`, rolled
into `overallStatus` (`:335`) and rendered on `/status` under the claim *"Component states above are
checked live against the Nxeon platform"* (`app/status/page.tsx:124-127`). Tautological for the page
itself, and false for the marketing site and admin console, neither of which is probed. `db`, `worker`
and `proxmox` **are** genuinely measured.

**19. "Server is ready" is Proxmox-task-deep only.** *PARTIAL.* `worker/index.ts:318` writes `RUNNING`
and `:323` notifies with an `ssh root@…` line straight after `waitForTask(startUpid)`. That proves
Proxmox accepted the start — not that the guest booted, cloud-init ran, or sshd is listening. The
cloud-init snippet write at `:274` is `.catch`'d, so a server can be reported ready with no cloud-init
applied.

**20. The API token scope badge contradicts the auth layer.** *PARTIAL.*
`components/customer/SecuritySettings.tsx:269` renders an empty-scopes token as **"read"** while
`lib/api-auth.ts:72` treats empty scopes as **full access**. Harmless only because the public API is
read-only; the footgun is documented in place at `lib/api-auth.ts:79-93`, and both halves must be dealt
with before any mutating endpoint ships.

**21. A provisioning knob no admin can see.** *THE INVERSE OF SAVED-BUT-UNREAD.*
`worker/index.ts:229` and `:476` read **`dedicated_ip_default`**, which is not in `SETTINGS_DEFAULTS`
and appears in no panel — so it silently defaults to `true` and every server gets a dedicated IP with no
operator control over it. This is the only survivor of the old "thirteen settings with no reader" gap,
and it is the more dangerous shape: a control that acts without a surface, rather than a surface that
does not act.

**22. Domain expiry can be locally invented.** *UNVERIFIED SUCCESS.*
`lib/actions-domains.ts:200`, `:219` (and the renewal path at `:325`):
`expiresAt: info.expires ?? new Date(Date.now() + dTerm.years × 365 × 86400_000)`. If the registrar

**23. Tax is configured and never charged.** *SAVED-BUT-UNREAD.* `applyTaxFromSettings`
(`lib/tax.ts:109`) has exactly one call site — `app/admin/products/page.tsx:93`, an admin MRR display.

warning is recorded in place at `lib/tax.ts:75-88`.

**24. `referral_reward_cents` is read by nothing.** *ENV-VS-SETTING SPLIT.* Validated in
`lib/actions-settings.ts:160` and defaulted to `"500"` in `lib/settings.ts:122`; the reward path reads
`process.env.REFERRAL_REWARD_CENTS` (`lib/growth.ts:14`), which is unset in `.env`. Editing the admin
field changes no payout — the same split that produced the domain-markup bug, and now the last one left.

**25. WHOIS privacy never reaches the registrar on a live domain, and the checklist does not say so.**
*PARTIAL.* `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts:133-152` writes the DB flag and makes no registrar call. The
action itself is honest — it returns *"Preference saved (on/off). WHOIS privacy at {registrar} is
provisioned at registration — contact support to change it on a live domain."* — and privacy **is**
